questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The variety of courses offered in the field of philosophy and the professors who taught the courses were well known and expert in their field.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The university of British Columbia is a high performance university, were your skills are being challenged. However, very motivating and the courses are flexible in the grading system depending on the professor.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The information was easy to find, as the university made everything very clear for exchange students. A whole team only advising exchange students was fairly easy to get in contact with

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The GoGlobal office was only dedicated to help with every part of the exchange experience of exchange students, thus they helped with issues regarding housing, health care and acedemic issues.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Up to 6 different student dorms were available. One could choose from single bedroom, to four bedroom and even living with more people. At the end it was chosen for you which dorm and room you were assigned to. However only 60% from the exchange students are getting a place, the other 40% have to find housing themselves.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: There were meal plan options, but mostly only for students who lived in dorms without a kitchen. These meal plans were quite expensive, but gave opportunity to eat at cantines at campus and reduced prices at other cafes and restaurants on campus.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It is prefarable to get housing on campus as the campus is huge itself and it takes up to one hour commute time with the bus, if someone is living in Vancouver. Thus, campus has a variety of food oppurtunities and cafes, which makes it easier to eat outside, than to cook at home, as the grocery prices are extremely high.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The Ponderosa Commons dorm was exceptionally good.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There were a lot of information sessions from the university and everything was explained step by step, which made the process fairly easy.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Due to the changes in the system, the new platform that we had to register for courses and have a overview of the expenses and finances was 'workday'. This was easy to manage, as on the portal we were able to register for course way in advance and were able to see whether we are accepted to the courses or currently in the waiting list. It was also possible to change courses after the first week, and try different courses.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Again, the GoGlobal office was there to help about registration issues either thorugh e-mail or in person appointments.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was quite successful and got 3/4 courses I really wanted, however some other courses are overfilled which is then hard to get in as an exchange student. However, often one was able to attend the class still and if the professor noticed active participation then it was possible to take the course

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: To sign up for courses as soon as possible to be able to be one of the first signed up, as well as attend courses even though one is listed on the waiting list. This makes it more likely to be able to take the course at the end.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was very challenging and a lot of information in a short time, but also very satisfied with the course materials as the professors were experts in their field and knowledge.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I was taking 4x 400-level courses, which is very comparable to MA courses. The level is quite high and can not be compared with introductory courses

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The biggest differences were the type of learning and examination. Almost all of my exams were hand written and professors did not use any digital devices to teach, and did not allow devices during the lecture and seminar. This is very different to UCPH teaching

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Philosophy of Mind 
Philosophy of Perception 
Conceptions of the Self 
Sociology of the Environment

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Definitely 'Conceptions of the Self' with Edward Slingerland. This course was highly informative and a lot of books were read in Eastern as well as Western philosophy. The professor was one of the best professors I had and very famous in his fields, having written multiple books for the public

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Washing card and topping up money for the washing

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Groceries were very expensive, while coffee and food on campus was more cheap

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Except for the competitive sport clubs, everything was available for exchange students and over 200 clubs that one could join

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A lot of events during the months were available, from free pancakes and burgers outside on campus to ice hockey and football games and more.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: American Football games are a cultural highlight as well as ice hockey games.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
A lot of hiking trips in the mountains either through bus and seabus, or with a rented car. 
Going to ski in the winter semester and to visit the cinemas and parks in the city

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy as the university is very international and multicultural. Some differences in tipping and politness in buses had to be adjusted to, however those were rather positive than negative.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Go to the events, and make sure to be in a group with other exchange students to experience the term together. Also do not miss on the events posted by the sports clubs and acedemic talks on campus

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The tipping was a bit confusing as it is normally expected to tip 15% to 20%, however as this is quite a bit for a student it was not always sure if this must be done or not.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The politness of the candians. Even if people would exist the bus in the back, everyone would thank the bus driver for driving them. People were looking out for eachother, and were not shy to

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Be sure to be ready for a possible tough semester depending on the courses you take! Be sure to sign up early for housing to have a higher chance to be living on campus. Think beforehand how much money you want or can spend, as it might be a bit more expensive. Be sure to make the best out of the nature around the area

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be sure to have all neccesary travel documents when arriving in Canada and a physical credit card for the washing machines on campus

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The courses as they were challenging but also very intersting and being able to live on your own and with international students so far away from home in a new culture.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The management of courses and free time, and handling expenses

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: I highly recommend anyone to go to UBC! What a wonderful experience for the self and the career!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
